metadata.title: Parallelized Stochastic Gradient Descent (Zinkevich et al., 2010)
metadata.framework: Parallel SGD by distributing data across workers, running SGD independently on each, and averaging the resulting models
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Zinkevich et al. (2010). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: Distributed optimization setting
nodes.statement: Minimize $f(w) = \mathbb{E}_{z \sim \mathcal{D}}[\ell(w, z)]$ where data is distributed across $K$ machines, each with access to a subset of the data (IID partition). The goal is to minimize communication while achieving the same convergence as centralized SGD.

nodes.name: One-shot averaging (parallel SGD)
nodes.statement: Each of $K$ workers independently runs SGD on its local data partition for $T$ steps starting from the same initial point $w_0$, producing local models $w_k^T$. The final model is the average: $\bar{w} = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{k=1}^{K} w_k^T$. Communication happens only once (at the end).

nodes.name: Convergence of averaged SGD
nodes.statement: For convex Lipschitz functions, one-shot parallel SGD with averaging achieves $\mathbb{E}[f(\bar{w}) - f(w^*)] = O(1/\sqrt{KT})$, matching the rate of centralized SGD on the full dataset of $KT$ examples. The averaging reduces variance by a factor of $K$.

nodes.name: Parallel SGD algorithm
nodes.statement: (1) Distribute data equally across $K$ workers. (2) Each worker initializes at $w_0$. (3) Each worker runs $T$ steps of SGD independently on local data. (4) Collect all $K$ final models. (5) Output $\bar{w} = \frac{1}{K} \sum_k w_k^T$.

nodes.name: Minimal communication
nodes.statement: One-shot averaging requires only a single round of communication (collecting final models). This is optimal for communication but may lose convergence speed compared to more frequent synchronization.

nodes.name: IID data assumption
nodes.statement: The analysis assumes data is IID across workers (random partition of a centralized dataset). The theory does not address non-IID data distributions, which is the setting addressed by federated learning.
